display.purpose: Cover titles on every page, the Overview's exposure total, the detail panel code, the report period and the next-due day numerals; 108% width; 2rem on phones.

display-lg.purpose: The obligation code on its entry page cover, the one size above display; 2.75rem on phones.

key-figure.purpose: The state figures on the Overview cover, the cost of a delay and the report key figures; tabular, 108% width.

headline.purpose: Reading-page section heads in navy with a hairline beneath, the entry page cost head and the planner result heads.

title.purpose: Block heads (By law, the list head, the day heading, Next due dates, empty states); the obligation name at 550; ledes at 400 and 1.5.

body.purpose: Running text; prose capped at 70ch at a 1.6 line height.

body-sm.purpose: Tables, detail sections, notes, the cover sub line and the footer.

figure.purpose: The figure voice: obligation codes in navy and counts, tabular figures.

control.purpose: Buttons, segmented options (700 when selected), law and filter chips and footer links; tabs and disclosure summaries at 650.

label.purpose: Column heads, field labels, section labels, meta lines and law tags in Slate Ink; sentence case, never uppercase; pills at 600.

chart.purpose: Lane counts and the cost-of-delay axes; timeline ticks at 500 (650 major) and Today at 700 in Cobalt.

mono.purpose: Fragment Mono for code identifiers only, on a Tag Grey chip; never for numbers.

shadows.name: control-lift
shadows.purpose: Resting lift on secondary buttons, inputs, selects and the file check; dropped by quiet and disabled buttons, every button on navy, and print.

shadows.name: segmented-thumb
shadows.purpose: The sliding thumb of the segmented control: the control lift plus a Control Rule ring.

shadows.name: primary-lift
shadows.purpose: The one cobalt primary in an action group, standing a little forward of its neighbors.

shadows.name: float
shadows.purpose: The timeline tooltip, the cost-of-delay readout, the report sheet on screen, and a source card under the pointer.

shadows.name: sheet
shadows.purpose: Right-hand dialogs, over the rgba(16, 24, 40, 0.42) scrim.

shadows.name: masthead-edge
shadows.purpose: A faint light hairline where the masthead meets the cover; a rule, not depth.

shadows.name: input-focus-halo
shadows.purpose: Focus state of text inputs, with a Cobalt border; a state signal, not depth.

shadows.name: band-figure-on
shadows.purpose: A key figure toggled on, over Cover Blue at 16%; a state signal on navy.

shadows.name: swatch-ring-on-navy
shadows.purpose: Rings a law swatch on the cover so dark law hues stay visible on navy.

shadows.name: calendar-selected
shadows.purpose: The selected day in the month grid, over Cobalt Wash.

shadows.name: file-ring
shadows.purpose: Transient: settles out of the file check when an item is marked filed; removed under reduced motion.

motion.name: ease-out
motion.purpose: The system ease: every state change, entrance and glide. Script counts use the matching exponential curve.

motion.name: ease-in-out
motion.purpose: Loops only: the ambient light on the cover and the loading shimmer.

motion.name: ease-exit
motion.purpose: Leaving: a closing sheet and its scrim, and the outgoing page in a view transition.

motion.name: dur-instant
motion.purpose: Press feedback (buttons, chips and key figures to 97%, the file check to 90%) and readout tracking.

motion.name: dur-fast
motion.purpose: Color, border and shadow on hover and focus; tooltip entrance and glide; the exit of a sheet.

motion.name: dur-base
motion.purpose: Changes of state: pills crossfading, marks recoloring, the lane tint, a filed row fading, the hover bar under a tab, small panels and disclosures rising in, new marks popping in.

motion.name: dur-slow
motion.purpose: Entrances and glides: rise-in, the segmented thumb, timeline marks and ticks moving, the detail panel and sheets sliding in, a new month or headline, the tab indicator between pages.

motion.name: dur-focal
motion.purpose: The focal draw: the Today line, and the cost-of-delay wash fading in behind its curve.

motion.name: rise-in
motion.value: 380ms ease-out from translateY(10px) and opacity 0, staggered 18 to 50ms
motion.purpose: The standard entrance for cover heads, key figures, aside items, day lists, leaves and report rows; content stays visible if it never runs.

motion.name: timeline-assemble
motion.value: 520ms ease-out from up to 96px toward Today at scale 0.4, delayed up to 260ms by distance
motion.purpose: The focal entrance of the Overview; with the Today line, in place within 800ms.

motion.name: timeline-pop
motion.purpose: Marks that appear after the first layout.

motion.name: delay-draw
motion.purpose: The cost-of-delay curve drawing itself once.

motion.name: flip-rows
motion.value: 380ms ease-out glide; new rows 320ms from translateY(8px), 18ms apart up to 260ms; first 120 rows
motion.purpose: Table rows moving to their new places when the order or filters change.

motion.name: count-up
motion.value: 520ms (700ms for the exposure total), exponential ease-out
motion.purpose: Key figures and report figures counting to new values.

motion.name: view-transition
motion.value: old page 160ms ease-exit fade; new page 360ms ease-out rising 12px; cover morph 420ms; tab indicator 380ms
motion.purpose: Page to page: the masthead holds, the cover morphs, the current-tab bar slides.

motion.name: sheet
motion.value: in 380ms ease-out from translateX(32px) and opacity 0 via @starting-style; out 160ms ease-exit
motion.purpose: Right-hand dialogs, with the scrim fading to rgba(16, 24, 40, 0.42) on the same timing.

motion.name: filed-confirmation
motion.value: check draws in 420ms after 60ms; a 10px Filed Green ring settles out in 700ms; the row holds Filed Tint, fading over 1100ms
motion.purpose: Marking an item filed from the table.

motion.name: band-light
motion.purpose: The ambient light on the cover; paused unless the cover is on screen.

motion.name: skeleton
motion.purpose: Loading shimmer: the selection blue at 55% and white sweeping across Cool Panel Grey.

motion.name: reduced-motion
motion.value: animations 200ms with no delay; transitions limited to color, background, border, opacity, fill, stroke and outline color at 120ms
motion.purpose: prefers-reduced-motion: spatial keyframes become fades, loops and the ring stop, view-transition groups do not animate, counts and row moves are instant; the filed tint keeps 1100ms.

breakpoints.name: split
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: the table and aside stack, the detail opens as a sheet, the entry page stacks.

breakpoints.name: masthead-wrap
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: tabs take their own row and scroll behind a right-edge fade.

breakpoints.name: phone
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: the cover and titles step down, key figures form a grid, rows stack, the month grid shows dots, next-due leaves scroll sideways.

breakpoints.name: timeline-narrow
breakpoints.purpose: Chart container width: short lane names, smaller marks, two-digit years, no counts or callout.

breakpoints.name: profile-compact
breakpoints.purpose: max-width: the profile button keeps only its icon.

breakpoints.name: delay-ticks
breakpoints.purpose: Cost-of-delay container width: the 30-day tick drops out.

breakpoints.name: delay-compact
breakpoints.purpose: Cost-of-delay container width: the plot shortens from 196px to 156px.

narrative.overview:
The compliance year is typeset the way a listed company sets its annual report. A deep navy masthead runs straight into a navy cover band at the top of every page, carrying the page's title, a short lede and, where the page has them, its key figures. Below the cover the working pages are white, and the content is ruled tables with tabular figures, short lists under section rules, and two charts: one shows how the horizon's deadlines fall law by law, the other what a single filing costs for each day it is late. The register is corporate and clean: a document the board would accept, read at a desk and equally at home on a phone between meetings. Density is high but calm. One working page carries a cover, a row of controls, a full-width chart and a long table without crowding, because separation comes from hairlines, tonal bands and generous section spacing rather than from boxes.

Color is held back so that it can carry meaning. Navy is the ink of record: the masthead and cover, every obligation code, the headline figures, the rule that opens each section, and every ordinary due date on the chart. A single cobalt marks what can be acted on or what is selected on white, and a lighter Cover Blue does that job on navy. Four muted state hues (overdue red, due-soon amber, extension blue, filed green) appear only where the state itself is the message. Nine law hues name the laws, but only as small squares and faint washes beside ink text, so a reader can follow one law across the chips, the chart's lanes and the tags without color ever standing in for words. Type is one family, Archivo, separated into roles by weight and, for the few largest lines, by width: bold headings, a heavier figure voice for codes and figures, a slightly wide display voice for cover titles and key figures, regular prose. Depth is nearly absent; surfaces are flat and tonal, and shadow only lifts a control or floats a transient layer.

Motion is refined and present everywhere, but it explains change rather than performing: a press answers at once, rows glide to their new places, figures count to their new values, and between pages the masthead holds while the cover morphs. Each surface has at most one authored moment; on the Overview it is the timeline assembling outward from Today. The system replaces a dark catalog look the user tried and rejected, and it refuses the pastel SaaS dashboard of count tiles. The product's confirmed rejections carry into the visual system: no alarm red everywhere, no walls of legal text, nothing playful or gamified, which is why motion confirms a filing and never celebrates it.
keyCharacteristics: A navy masthead running into a navy cover band on every page, over white working pages and cool grey panels; light only.
Ruled tables with tabular figures; hairlines, not boxes, separate content.
A 2px navy rule opens every working section.
One cobalt for action and selection on white, Cover Blue for selection on navy; state hues only where state is the message.
Nine law hues as identity, held to small squares and faint washes beside ink text.
One family (Archivo): 700 headings, a 750 figure voice, and a 108% width for the largest lines.
Two charts: the swimlane timeline, its marks sized by the cost of filing late, and the cost-of-delay curve.
Flat surfaces; shadow only for control lift, floating layers and dialogs.
Motion that confirms and continues on one exponential ease-out, with a reduced-motion path of fades.

rules.name: The One Cobalt Rule
rules.body: Cobalt is the only hue that means act or selected on white: primary buttons, links, toggled chips, the selected row, day and range, focus, and Today on the chart. Nothing decorative is cobalt. Two selections are marked differently, both deliberate: on navy, selection is Cover Blue (the current tab's bar, a toggled key figure), and the segmented control shows its current value as a raised white thumb with navy text.

rules.name: The State Is the Message Rule
rules.body: Red, amber, extension blue and green appear only on an element whose message is that state: status pills, timeline marks, the key-figure dots on the cover that serve as their legend, calendar code chips, the file check and the confirmation of a filing, the extension note, and status cells and figures in the report. Never as a section color, heading color, row stripe or page wash.

rules.name: The Quiet Red Rule
rules.body: Red means overdue and nothing else. The Overdue key figure turns red (Overdue Red on Navy) only when it is above zero, and so does the report's Overdue figure; with nothing overdue, the only red left on screen is the Overdue figure's legend dot.

rules.name: The Law Swatch Rule
rules.body: A law hue appears only beside the law's name in ink, as a square swatch with 2px corners, a faint wash, a lane tint or the cost-of-delay curve. It never colors text, never fills a circle and never stands for a state: squares name laws, and circles belong to state and data.

rules.name: The Figure Voice Rule
rules.body: Codes, counts and figures take the figure voice (750, -0.02em, tabular figures), and the largest of them also open to the 108% width. Dates and amounts in tables take 650 with tabular figures, and every table is tabular by default. Obligation codes are navy unless a state chip recolors them, a filed row fades them or the cover sets them white.

rules.name: The Sentence-Case Label Rule
rules.body: Labels are 0.78125rem (12.5px) at 650 and +0.01em, in sentence case, in Slate Ink; secondary labels drop to Caption Slate. No uppercase, no wide tracking, no small caps.

rules.name: The One Family Rule
rules.body: Archivo carries every role, from the 3.5rem entry code to the chart's 11px axis text, at two widths: normal (100%) for text, and 108% for display, display large and key figures. The wordmark's lockup is its own setting (104%). Never reach for the condensed widths, add a second display face, or set numbers in Fragment Mono.

rules.name: The Ruled Section Rule
rules.body: A working section opens with a 2px navy rule across its full width (the chart, each aside list, the detail panel, the calendar's day list, the entry page's cost section and aside lists, the report's key figures), and its rows are divided by 1px Hairline Rules. Boxes are the exception, never the container.

rules.name: The Cover Rule
rules.body: Every page opens with the navy cover under the masthead: the page title in display type, a lede or sub line in muted white, and at most one row of key figures under a 1px white rule. The cover says what the page is about; the work itself always starts on white below it.

rules.name: The Paper Flat Rule
rules.body: Content does not float. Tables, lists, leaves, panels and the charts lie flat on the page; only controls, tooltips, the on-screen report sheet and dialogs carry shadow, and a card that is wholly a link may rise into the float under the pointer as its hover state.

rules.name: The Round Ends Rule
rules.body: Full pills belong to statuses and filter chips. Buttons that do something (file, print, export, subscribe, save) are 6px rectangles, and so are the key figures that filter by state.

rules.name: The Two Charts Rule
rules.body: The system has two charts, each answering one question: the swimlane timeline (which law is heaviest when, and which filing costs most if late) and the cost-of-delay curve (what one filing costs for each day it is late). The costliest list's 3px bars compare amounts inside a list and are not a chart. No sparklines, rings, gauges or further charts; other surfaces show the same data as ruled tables, the month grid and lists.

rules.name: The One Entrance Rule
rules.body: Each surface gets at most one authored moment: on the Overview, the timeline's marks assembling outward from Today while the Today line draws itself, in place within 800ms; wherever the cost-of-delay chart appears, its curve drawing once. Everything else enters by rising 8 to 12px into place (320 to 380ms for content, 240ms for small panels and disclosures) in staggers of 18 to 50ms, or by fading, and every element is readable at its end state if the animation never runs.

rules.name: The Continuity Rule
rules.body: Motion explains change: rows glide from their old places when the order or filters change, figures count to new values, the segmented thumb slides to the new option, marks and ticks glide to a new horizon, a new month slides in from the side it came from, and between pages the masthead holds while the cover morphs and the tab indicator slides. An island that replaces a static page never repeats the entrance it inherits, and the cover's ambient light runs only while the cover is on screen. Under reduced motion, movement goes: entrances become fades of 200ms, transitions keep only color and opacity, loops stop, counts land at once, rows jump and pages crossfade; the filed confirmation keeps its green tint at full length.

dos: Do open every page with the navy cover under the masthead, and every working section below it with the 2px navy rule, dividing rows with 1px Hairline Rules (#e2e7ee).

Do keep Cobalt (#1d4ed8) for the primary action, links, toggled chips, selection, focus and Today on white, and Cover Blue (#8fb0ff) for selection on navy, with at most one primary button per action group.
Do name a law with its swatch (a square with 2px corners in the law's hue) beside the law's name in ink.
Do set codes, counts and figures in the figure voice (750, -0.02em, tabular figures), keep codes navy on white, and give only the largest lines the 108% width.

Do show state with a pill, a dot or a mark in the state's color, and use the state's text tone (overdue-text, soon-text, extended-text, filed-text, and overdue-on-navy on the cover) for any state-colored text.
Do leave an ordinary upcoming item navy and pill-less in tables and lists; color is for exceptions.
Do put legal text, penalty bases and change notes behind a disclosure, and show every rule's sources with its verified date.
Do draw icons from the Lucide set at 16px with a 1.75 stroke, round caps and joins, in the current text color; the calendar-check mark is the product's own.
Do theme the browser's own surfaces from the palette: #d6e2ff selection, a thin #c3cbd6 scrollbar, a Cobalt caret, 1px Cobalt Line underlines offset 0.2em, and Cobalt checkboxes and sliders.

Do time motion from the scale: 110ms for a press, 160ms for color and hover, 240ms for a change of state, 380ms for entrances and glides and 720ms for the one focal draw, on the ease-out cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1); exits run faster on cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 1, 1), and loops on cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1).
Do start every animation from a readable end state and give every movement a reduced-motion form, a fade or nothing.
donts: Don't bring back a dark ground or the dark catalog look this system replaced; the navy cover is a band at the top of a light page, never a theme.

Don't build metric tiles. Counts and totals set large belong on the navy cover and in the report's key figures, as figures over labels with no box, icon or trend arrow; on white, a large figure is either a chart's readout (the cost of a delay) or a date (the next-due leaves).
Don't use red for anything but overdue, and don't color a count red at zero.
Don't add a second accent hue, or use a state hue as decoration, a section color, a row stripe or a page wash.
Don't set text in a law hue, fill a circle with one, or let a law hue stand for a state.
Don't make cards the page structure or nest boxes; working content lives in ruled sections and hairline rows, and bordered panels stay limited to the cases under Cards / Containers.
Don't add a third chart, sparklines or progress rings.
Don't uppercase or letter-space labels, and don't set numbers in Fragment Mono; it is for code identifiers only.
Don't use Archivo's condensed widths, go wider than the 108% display width, or add a second display face.
Don't lift content with shadow or raise anything on hover that is not itself clickable; only controls, tooltips, the on-screen report sheet, dialogs and a link card under the pointer carry shadow.

Don't add gradient fills, gradient text, glass or blur; the only gradients in the system are functional (the select caret, the loading shimmer, the masthead's scroll fade) and the cover's ambient light.
Don't celebrate a filing with confetti, illustrations or emoji; the check draws itself, a ring settles out of it and the row holds a brief green tint, then the item goes quiet.
Don't set white text on the amber due-soon solid; amber carries text as soon-text on its tint, and cluster counts on amber marks are Ledger Ink.
Don't replay an entrance when an island replaces a static page, keep a decorative loop running off screen, or use bounce, elastic or overshooting curves.
